input: events contains n [start,end,value] rows with 0 <= start <= end <= 1000000000 and nonnegative safe values. Require twice the maximum value to be safe and n+1 within collection bounds. Empty input is accepted. Collections are ordinary finite dense arrays/lists, not subclasses, proxies, sparse/accessor-backed collections. Strings are ordinary/primitive strings. Every collection length and computed allocation size fits [0,4294967295], with padded sizes explicitly included. No concurrent mutation or built-in monkey-patching is allowed. Preconditions are not runtime-checked, and allocation/resource capacity or completion is not guaranteed by declared bounds. JavaScript integer inputs are primitive safe-integer Number, excluding negative zero, NaN, infinities, fractions and BigInt.
return: Maximum value from attending at most two non-overlapping closed intervals. Equal end/start times overlap, so the second start must be strictly greater than the first end.
mutation_aliasing: Inputs and caller-held aliases remain unchanged; working state is private. The Solution instance retains no state. Sorting copies the outer event array; original event rows are never changed.
numeric: Upper bound compares start directly with end without end+1 arithmetic. Value sums fit the twice-maximum bound; timestamp comparator differences are at most 1000000000. All integer inputs/intermediates remain within [-9007199254740991,9007199254740991]; no bitwise coercion is used.
complexity: O(n log(n+1)+1) time and O(n+1) auxiliary space for copied events, starts, padded suffix maxima and sort workspace. Bounds include ordinary built-in operations/allocations and assume bounded-word arithmetic, constant-time indexing, amortized append/pop and any explicitly stated hash/sort behavior.
